chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Ihram is from five Mawaqit (stations of entering the state of Ihram) which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated. It is not appropriate for a pilgrim or a visitor to enter Ihram before them or after them. He designated Dhu al-Hulayfah for the people of Medina, which is Masjid al-Shajara, where he prays and assumes the state of Ihram for Hajj. He designated Al-Juhfah for the people of Syria. He designated Al-Aqiq for the people of Najd. He designated Qarn al-Manazil for the people of Ta'if. He designated Yalamlam for the people of Yemen. And it is not appropriate for anyone to prefer [deviate] from the Mawaqit of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.الْإِحْرَامُ: Ihram (ritual state of consecration for Hajj/Umrah)
key_terms.الْجُحْفَةَ: Al-Juhfah (the Miqat for people of Syria)
key_terms.الْعَقِيقَ: Al-Aqiq (the Miqat for people of Najd)
key_terms.ذَا الْحُلَيْفَةِ: Dhu al-Hulayfah (the Miqat for people of Medina)
key_terms.قَرْنَ الْمَنَازِلِ: Qarn al-Manazil (the Miqat for people of Ta'if)
key_terms.يَلَمْلَمَ: Yalamlam (the Miqat for people of Yemen)

ai.seo_question: What are the five Mawaqit for Ihram in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the five specific Miqat stations established by the Prophet Muhammad for pilgrims from various regions, emphasizing the binding nature of these boundaries for both Hajj and Umrah. It underscores the scholarly principle that deviating from these divinely sanctioned locations invalidates the proper observance of the pilgrimage rites, reflecting the structured order of Islamic worship.
